claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation will promote formation of an oxide layer on a CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy surface.
The pre-formed oxide layer will be coherent, thin, adherent, and lubricious.
The oxide tribolayer will be self-healing during tribological service.
The oxide tribolayer will likely be enriched in oxide-forming elements already present in the alloy.
For CrMnFeCoNi, manganese is a likely oxide-forming element.
The oxide tribolayer will act as a barrier between the contacting surfaces.
The oxide layer will reduce interfacial shear strength.
The oxide layer will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
Reduced shear strength and metal-to-metal contact will lower both coefficient of friction and wear rate.
The oxide film will remain stable enough to provide lubrication from room temperature to approximately 800 °C.
Relative to untreated alloy, pre-oxidation may reduce coefficient of friction by approximately 50%.
Relative to untreated alloy, pre-oxidation may reduce wear rate by approximately one order of magnitude.
The predicted improvements depend on the oxide film remaining intact and stable.
Moderately oxidizing environments will support effectiveness by permitting stable oxide formation.
The intervention may be compromised in fully inert atmospheres because the oxide film cannot form or be maintained.
Aggressive chemical environments may rapidly degrade the oxide layer and compromise the intervention.
Untreated specimens tested under otherwise identical conditions constitute the experimental control.

The hypothesis is falsified if pre-oxidized specimens fail to show statistically significant reductions in both friction and wear across the tested temperature range, or if their oxide layer is unstable or non-adherent.
